newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka suspends policemen for refusing war duty.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka suspends policemen for refusing war duty.

text.p: Sri Lankan authorities have suspended 234 policemen for refusing to do "bunker duty" in the island's north where government forces are battling separatist rebels, a Colombo newspaper reported on Sunday.

The Sunday Leader said the policemen refused to be deployed to bunkers along the northern Vavuniya-Mannar road, captured by the military from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels last February.
The LTTE, which controlled the 100 km (60 mile) road, were pushed to the north of the road and the rebels are still active in areas just to the north.
"These policemen will be charged under the police ordinance for cowardice," the newspaper quoted Gamini Silva, senior superintendent of police for the north-central Vavuniya region, as saying.
Military officials told Reuters the men were moved to the area from their stations in the east to relieve soldiers who would take part in a major military offensive against the rebels in the north.
The military is believed to be preparing for an offensive to open a land route linking Vavuniya, 220 km (140 miles) north of Colombo, with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The military now relies entirely on air and sea transport to send troops and supplies to bases in Jaffna, because most of the Wanni region north of Vavuniya is under rebel control.
Residents of Vavuniya say they have seen a large scale military build-up in recent days close to the army's forward defences just north of Vavuniya.
Residents say at least three schools in the area have been ordered to close in order to house troops and policemen who have been arriving to take part in the offensive.
The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, have also said they are prepared to face an offensive.
The government says more than 50,000 have died in the war, now in its 14th year, although the Tigers say the death toll is higher.
